title: Thermodynamics of photonic nonlinear Aharonov-Bohm cages
abstract: We investigate equilibrium and non-equilibrium thermodynamics of one-dimensional photonic diamond lattices with Kerr nonlinearity. The equilibrium phase diagram is obtained as a function of the synthetic magnetic flux acting on each plaquette. In the linear regime, the magnetic flux can induce Aharonov-Bohm caging, flattening all Bloch bands and suppressing particle and energy currents. In this caging regime, non-vanishing currents are enabled by nonlinearity. By imposing stationary temperature- and chemical potential- imbalances at the system boundaries, we show that at weak nonlinearity fine tuning the flux at the Aharonov-Bohm caging transforms the system from a conductor to an insulator. For intermediate nonlinear strength, the system remains conducting for all magnetic fluxes; however, the caging condition significantly enhances the Seebeck coefficient and thermoelectric figure of merit, improving the thermoelectric features of the system. Our results give evidence of a novel route towards optimization of coupled transport devices, based on the control of linear versus nonlinear conduction channels via a synthetic magnetic flux.
summary: This paper analyzes the thermodynamics and transport properties of nonlinear photonic lattices subjected to an artificial magnetic flux. By controlling this flux, the system can be tuned from a conductor to an insulator, or its thermoelectric efficiency can be significantly enhanced. The methodology combines advanced statistical mechanics with quantum transport theory.
main_problem: The study investigates the equilibrium and non-equilibrium thermodynamics of photonic lattices exhibiting Kerr nonlinearity, focusing on how a synthetic magnetic flux controls transport properties.
main_result: Tuning the synthetic magnetic flux can transform the system between conducting and insulating states at weak nonlinearity, while intermediate nonlinearities significantly enhance thermoelectric performance by optimizing current channels.
method: The authors employ thermodynamic formalism, linear response theory (Onsager relations), and Landauer theory to calculate transport coefficients like conductivity and Seebeck coefficient.
model_or_system: The system is a quasi 1D photonic diamond lattice threaded by a synthetic magnetic flux ($\phi$) and possessing local Kerr nonlinearity ($\gamma$). The dynamics are analyzed using coupled field equations derived from the Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Average norm density ($a$), energy density ($h$), heat current, norm current ($j_a$), Seebeck coefficient ($S$), and thermoelectric figure of merit ($ZT$).
important_parameters: Synthetic magnetic flux ($\phi$), nonlinear strength ($\gamma$), temperature/chemical potential imbalances ($ eta, \mu$). Key regimes include the linear limit ($\gamma=0$) and the Aharonov-Bohm caging condition ($\phi=\pi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes specific boundary conditions (Monte Carlo reservoirs) for non-equilibrium calculations and utilizes approximations like Gaussian integrals in normal mode expansions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate band structures showing flat bands at $\phi=\pi$, phase diagrams mapping accessible thermodynamic regions, and plots detailing the dependence of currents ($j_a, j_h$) on flux ($\phi$) and nonlinearity ($\gamma$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the model Hamiltonian and analyzing equilibrium states (phase diagrams). It then moves to non-equilibrium transport using Landauer theory and Onsager relations to quantify how $\phi$ and $\gamma$ control currents and thermoelectric efficiency.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, tunable platform—photonic lattices—to study fundamental concepts of quantum transport, including the interplay between geometric constraints (caging) and nonlinearity in optimizing energy conversion devices.
